title: Validate Binary Search Tree
keyIdea: A valid BST read in-order (left, node, right) gives strictly increasing values. Collect the in-order list and check every neighbour pair; or pass a (low, high) range down and check each node against it.

approaches.name: Range bounds while going down
approaches.idea: validate(node, low, high): node must be strictly inside (low, high). Left child gets (low, node), right child gets (node, high). Start with (LONG_MIN, LONG_MAX).
approaches.why: Each node is checked once; stops at the first bad node. long bounds avoid problems when a value is INT_MIN or INT_MAX.

approaches.name: In-order list must be increasing
approaches.idea: inorder() fills ans with the values in left-node-right order; any ans[i] >= ans[i + 1] means it's not a BST.
approaches.why: One traversal plus one pass over the list; the list holds all n values.

quiz.q: [5,4,6,null,null,3,7]: each parent–child pair looks fine. Valid?
options: No: 3 is in 5's right subtree but smaller than 5
Equal values aren't allowed: a BST needs strictly smaller left, strictly bigger right

quiz.q: Why does the bounds version use long instead of int?
options: A node can equal INT_MIN or INT_MAX, so the starting bounds must be outside the int range

quiz.q: In this in-order version, what would ans.size() - 1 do for an empty tree?
options: Wrap around to a huge number (size() is unsigned), but LeetCode never gives an empty tree
